entries.claim: The locally installed official @deepseek-ai/dsh package is version 0.1.0-rc.6, points to github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, and documents dsh web as the web-profile alias, but its public CLI documentation does not establish a stable user-owned Base URL field or a safe automatic-write adapter contract.

The first governed RU-003 verification run executed five scenarios successfully but the catalog scenario failed because invoking Vitest inside the mandatory read-only source sandbox attempted to create vitest.config.ts.timestamp-*.mjs in the project root. After replacing that nested runner with direct Node TypeScript module execution, local execution passed all six scenarios; redispatch was then blocked because the dispatcher revalidated the completed RU-002 dependency against RU-003's intentionally superseding current UI outputs.

Read-only audit reproduces native tcp443_reachable vs renderer tcp_443_reachable rejection. Desktop discovery discards Windows package launch identity. CLI open only shows instructions, Pi/Hermes success is stdout-nonempty, and restore errors fall through to misleading unchanged/restored copy.

Current code fixes Claude internal model to Sonnet, overwrites request models in both bridges, persists one model per tool, drops some SSE errors, imposes 60-second read idle, and waits unbounded for activation lock on quit. Windows credential blob limit is 2560 bytes.

The shared native activation command performs secure publication and atomic semantic readback, then synchronously runs seven different real-model verification paths with observed waits of 90, 120, 150 or 600 seconds; provider slowness therefore blocks the button and rolls back otherwise valid local configuration.

The installed DSH 0.1.2-rc.1 executable is a JavaScript launcher with #!/usr/bin/env node. The signed 0.4.10 assistant process has PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin, while DSH discovery canonicalizes its wrapper symlink to bin.js and the DSH adapter inherits the restricted GUI PATH and discards stderr. Running that same discovered target with the GUI PATH exits 127 because node is not found; running it from the terminal PATH returns a valid loopback web URL.

entries.claim: A no-network synthetic check using the installed Codex 0.153.4 binary, a loopback fixture and the same provider-scoped command-backed token shape reached /responses with the selected synthetic model and exact command token. Current source already preserves auth.json, writes model_provider=yeschoy and records only requests that enter the local bridge. Therefore the official account shown by Codex is not route evidence; the local bridge observation is the authoritative client-side receipt.

The current official Codex configuration reference documents ~/.codex/config.toml, model_providers.<id>.base_url, responses-only wire_api, and model_providers.<id>.auth.command as a command that prints a bearer token to stdout; auth.command must not be combined with env_key, experimental_bearer_token, or requires_openai_auth.

The current official Claude Code documentation identifies ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL as the custom endpoint setting and apiKeyHelper as a dynamic script-based credential source, supporting a preview of owned settings without placing a literal API key in settings.

The current official OpenCode provider documentation defines custom providers under provider.<id>, uses @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoints, accepts options.baseURL, and identifies model entries by their exact model IDs.

The current official Pi models documentation identifies ~/.pi/agent/models.json, provider baseUrl and api fields, exact model IDs, OpenAI-compatible API modes, and an apiKey value beginning with ! as a command evaluated at request time.

Claude supports full-ID inferenceModels with display-only labels; Codex loads a custom catalog at startup; OpenAI SDK uses a 600-second inference timeout default. These support bounded implementation choices, not live relay compatibility.

Current CC Switch normal provider switching validates and writes configuration without force-killing user applications, while its user guidance distinguishes reload behavior: Codex and Claude Desktop need a restart, and Claude Code commonly applies subsequent changes to a new session.

Current official Codex configuration documentation supports a provider-scoped command-backed bearer token, requires provider configuration in the user-level config, and forbids combining command auth with env_key, a literal bearer token or requires_openai_auth. The current CC Switch preservation guide likewise keeps the official login in auth.json, routes model traffic through config.toml, requires a restart, and says account display must not be used to judge billing or route selection.

RU-003 should add a deterministic beginner configuration-preview planner for the fixed five-tool catalog and the two product-approved line roots. It may show only evidenced target fields and derived protocol endpoints, must leave the model ID unavailable until a server catalog exists, and must block all configuration, credential, file-read, file-write, connectivity, and rollback actions until later backend, secure-helper, and exact-version evidence is frozen.

A verification-only successor release unit should preserve RU-003 product behavior and source exactly, use the corrected direct-module acceptance scenario under the mandatory read-only sandbox, retain the original failed run as historical evidence, and avoid replaying the dispatcher dependency check that compares intentionally superseded UI outputs to RU-002.

Replace seven adapter-specific blocking verification definitions with one activation state machine: validate eligibility, obtain native credentials, atomically commit and read back owned settings, start only helper-owned local runtimes, and handle desktop reload through explicit normal-quit consent. Observe the first real user request asynchronously instead of gating configuration on it.

RU-060 should supersede the 0.4.10 packaging authority without repackaging. It should preserve Codex official identity while making the actual Yeschoy bridge receipt explicit, retain exact gpt-6-astra routing even if the vendor UI abbreviates its display label, preserve non-destructive desktop restart semantics, and launch discovered Node-backed CLI wrappers with a closed runtime search path derived from the native-discovered wrapper chain so DSH and other supported agents work from a GUI process.
The mainland-optimized and Cloudflare global-acceleration lines share the same account, API key, model availability, and pricing semantics; only the network path differs.

The default model list shows models available to the current account and compatible with the selected tool; all models may be viewed with unavailable entries disabled and explained, and a removed model is never silently substituted.

The product owner accepted the exact-version compatibility allowlist for V1: automatic configuration is enabled only for exact tool versions that passed the complete matrix, while unknown, newly released, failed, and otherwise unverified versions remain read-only until a trusted compatibility update adds them.

The product owner authorized implementation to continue after RU-002 and accepted starting the next client-only one-click configuration foundation while preserving the decision not to modify NewAPI, servers, Nginx, DNS, databases, or production configuration in this phase.

The owner asks to resolve all findings in the preceding audit: diagnostics false error, Windows Codex launch, uneven application verification/daily opening, and incorrect restore-failure messages. Client-only work; preserve existing changes and do not mutate server or real account/tool settings during development.

decisions.question: How should the accepted RU-003 implementation be verified after the original frozen acceptance runner proved incompatible with mandatory read-only isolation and redispatch rechecked superseded dependency outputs?
decisions.choice: Create RU-004 as a verification-only successor to RU-003. Preserve the RU-003 product scope, source, contract, page, and blocked side-effect boundary without modification; execute the same six semantic scenarios using the corrected direct Node TypeScript module loader plus read-only source assertions; retain the original failed run as immutable historical evidence; and declare no work-package dependency because RU-004 changes no implementation and its release-unit dependency and supersession preserve the authority chain.

decisions.question: How should the client prove Codex uses Yeschoy while retaining official-app identity, and how should GUI-launched DSH and other npm agents resolve their runtime without depending on a terminal PATH?
decisions.choice: Keep Codex official identity and plugin state in auth.json, keep model routing exclusively in the user-level Yeschoy provider, and retain the officially supported provider-scoped command token rather than copying a literal key into config.toml. Treat only a request observed by the Yeschoy loopback bridge as route proof; label configuration-ready and route-confirmed as different states, show the exact forwarded model ID, and do not rewrite gpt-6-astra merely to defeat Codex UI abbreviation. For CLI tools, preserve the discovered wrapper while deduplicating by canonical identity, derive a bounded child-only PATH from its symlink chain, and apply it to DSH, terminal launch and isolated adapter checks. Keep existing normal-quit consent, atomic rollback, exact native target and no-paid-probe rules.

requirements.statement: RU-003 preserves RU-002 and adds a beginner-readable local configuration preview for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH across the mainland-optimized and global-accelerated lines without reading or changing any tool configuration, accessing a credential, contacting a server, or inventing a model ID.
acceptance: The configuration destination presents exactly Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, and DSH in stable order and lets the user choose exactly one tool for the current preview.
The line step presents exactly mainland optimized at https://yeschoy.com and global accelerated at https://api.yeschoy.com, and the selected line root remains visible in the summary.

Claude Code previews the approved root URL, Codex, OpenCode, and Pi preview the selected root with /v1, and DSH explicitly withholds a protocol endpoint and write target because its exact web-profile adapter is not verified.
The preview names only evidenced user-owned fields, exposes no literal secret or complete user path, and clearly states that it has not read an existing configuration.
Model ID remains visibly unavailable pending the first-party model catalog; the UI displays no sample model, guessed model, price, connectivity result, or supported-version claim.
The apply control remains disabled and the projection reports networkAttempted, configurationRead, configurationWritten, and credentialAccessed as false for every tool and line selection.
RU-001 local discovery and RU-002 account and billing readiness behavior remain available and unchanged, and no NewAPI, server, Nginx, DNS, database, updater, or production resource is modified.

requirements.statement: Repair cross-application diagnosis, platform launching, usable CLI opening and truthful verification/recovery without modifying servers or real user settings during development.
acceptance: Real Rust-serialized reachable/mixed/failure connectivity results are accepted by the renderer; stale, malformed, partial and invoke errors never invent network failures or lose valid per-line evidence.

Windows Store/MSIX discovery preserves validated package application identity; ordinary desktop executables remain supported and unsafe/unrelated launch targets are rejected. Initialization and daily opening share platform launcher.
CLI proof rejects banners/help/empty/failed output; typed process failures distinguish start, timeout, read/wait and nonzero execution; outputs/secrets never cross IPC.

All seven targets are offered launch-only opening after read-only validation; four CLI targets open a terminal using native-resolved paths without secrets or caller commands. Repeated open does not reconfigure or issue probes.
File or credential restoration failures are visible recovery-required states, never unchanged/restored success; account switch, stale reply and recovery journal boundaries remain intact.

All scoped regressions, renderer typecheck/production build and Windows compile are recorded separately from real platform/application acceptance. Internal 0.4.8 artifacts never imply complete live-user validation.

requirements.statement: Implement explicitly selected model sets with real identity and fixed per-model billing routes, honest request errors and cooperative bounded exit without packaging or server mutation.
acceptance: Up to the documented 200-entry catalog bound, unique full model IDs bind explicit billing groups; default is a member. No silent cross-group fallback or enrollment of unselected models. Legacy records upgrade on explicit activation only.

All seven adapters publish native model menus/catalogs via authenticated loopback routing; legitimate native default changes are not configuration corruption. In-flight requests retain their route. Unsupported optional vendor menus do not block default use.
Credential sets remain inside OS credential storage, handle the Windows per-blob bound transactionally, and never expose full keys through renderer, files, errors or diagnostics.

Claude identity uses real IDs rather than Sonnet display masking; both bridges route requested model exactly and isolate continuation history. Curated HTTP/SSE errors and in-memory last-request observations never turn failed streams into success.

Window close offers background/cancel/exit globally. Confirmed exit rejects new operations, cancels safe work, preserves in-flight account mutations and local rollback, and stops owned runtimes with bounded grace and recoverable progress.

Synthetic transaction/route/stream/exit tests, actual renderer tests/typecheck/build and Windows compilation pass. No installer, signed release, server change or live-account success is inferred from these tests.

requirements.statement: Make one-click activation fast and uniform for all seven supported agents by separating atomic local configuration from asynchronous real-model observation and by safely handling applications that must reload settings.
acceptance: All seven targets share one completion rule: exact account model/group eligibility, native secure credential storage, atomic owned-field commit and semantic readback, required helper-owned loopback readiness, and applicable open dispatch. The activation button never sends or waits for a paid upstream model prompt.

If Claude Desktop or Codex Desktop is already running, the first request returns application_running without account, key or file mutation. After an explicit save-work confirmation, native code requests normal quit, never force termination, stops if the app remains open, and reopens the exact discovered installation after success.

Claude Code, Pi, Hermes and OpenClaw never terminate an existing terminal or editor session and plainly state that a new session uses the new settings. DSH may reuse or restart only its assistant-owned runtime.

A successfully read-back configuration remains connected when the first real model request later reports upstream timeout, quota, model or provider failure; that observation appears in the existing recent-connection result and can guide model or line switching.

Synthetic native and renderer tests cover every adapter, running/not-running/refused desktop lifecycle branches, no-force-kill behavior, rollback/reopen behavior, truthful copy, and macOS Apple-Silicon plus Windows compilation without packaging.

requirements.statement: Make Codex route ownership independently verifiable and make DSH plus the supported Node-backed command-line agents launch correctly from the restricted macOS and Windows desktop environment without weakening credential or recovery boundaries.
acceptance: Codex continues to preserve the official auth.json identity and uses only the user-level model_provider=yeschoy configuration with mutually exclusive command-backed provider authentication. Synthetic current-version evidence proves that this exact shape reaches the selected loopback /responses route and token command instead of official model transport.

The setup and recent-request UI explicitly distinguishes an official Codex login identity from model traffic. Before a real application request arrives it says route use is not yet verified; after the local bridge records a completed request it says that Yeschoy relay use is confirmed and shows the exact forwarded model ID, group and line.

The product preserves exact model ID gpt-6-astra and explains that Codex may render its own shortened 6 Astra label. It does not alias or rewrite the upstream model merely to alter vendor UI text and never infers model identity from assistant self-description.

Native CLI discovery deduplicates by canonical identity but retains the executable wrapper selected from PATH or a closed common directory. Launch code constructs a child-only runtime search path from that wrapper and its bounded symlink chain, so a GUI process can resolve npm-provided node without changing global PATH or accepting renderer paths or commands.

DSH web starts through its canonical profile entry point, accepts only a validated loopback startup URL, reuses only the assistant-owned runtime, opens the system browser, and completes or fails within a bounded interval without a paid model probe. The same runtime-path rule is applied to the supported CLI verification and terminal launch paths.

Synthetic native and renderer tests cover restricted GUI PATH, symlinked Node launchers, invalid or hostile paths, DSH startup/reuse/failure, Codex route copy and exact recent-request evidence. Typecheck, production renderer build, strict Rust checks, Apple-Silicon compile and Windows x64 compile pass without packaging or changing server, NewAPI, billing, updater or vendor binaries.

A configuration write cannot commit without a recovery snapshot and external-change check. DEC-078 authorizes one encrypted pre-connection baseline per tool until explicit restoration; no backup history.

Native code accepts only two compiled active line IDs, seven closed target IDs, exact current-account model/group bindings and an optional native installation handoff. restartRunningApp is accepted only for Claude Desktop or Codex Desktop after the renderer shows an explicit save-work confirmation; it authorizes a normal quit request and reopen, never force termination. Keys remain native.

A same-tool pending encrypted transaction is recovered first; completed records are never auto-restored. A running desktop app returns application_running before account, key or file mutation unless the confirmed restart flag is present. Configuration ready is recomputed from atomic write/readback and local runtime readiness, not a paid model reply.
contracts.compatibility: Wire schema remains version 4. The optional restartRunningApp boolean defaults false and application_running is a new closed outcome. Existing model catalogs, exact model/group routing, connection receipts and first-request diagnostics remain compatible. CLI tools keep current sessions untouched and take effect in a new session; Claude Desktop and Codex Desktop may be normally quit and reopened after explicit confirmation.

errorSemantics: Invalid target, active line, model, billing group, installation identity or restart flag fails before key acquisition or file access.

A synchronous ready result requires the target credential in native secure storage, atomic configuration commit with semantic readback, the required helper-owned loopback runtime listening, and an applicable desktop or DSH open dispatch. It never waits for or bills an upstream model request.

Claude Desktop and Codex Desktop are checked again under the activation lock. If running and restartRunningApp is absent, application_running returns before mutation. With explicit consent native code requests a normal quit, waits only for a bounded exit, never force-terminates, and reopens only the exact discovered target.

A refused or incomplete normal quit leaves settings untouched and returns application_running with graceful_restart_required. CLI tools never terminate an existing terminal or editor session; their new configuration applies to a new session. Only helper-owned runtimes may be restarted.

Configuration, secure-storage, local-runtime and launch failures remain distinct closed outcomes. A failing local transaction restores touched files and prior credentials and deletes only a newly created token whose ownership is proven; a desktop app normally closed for the attempt is reopened against restored settings.

After ready, the first real application request is observed by the existing local gateway and exposed through recent connection results. An upstream timeout, quota, model or provider error does not roll back a configuration that was already atomically installed.
Complete keys never cross renderer IPC, appear in ordinary configuration or enter diagnostic text. Loopback compatibility endpoints return only public model metadata and health state.
Duplicate or unregistered model/group is rejected; no implicit default/group substitution. Cancellation before local write is safe; after write must restore locally or retain recovery state.

An installer handoff atomically consumes its one-use intent before credential or configuration work, checks full selection and exact installed target, and uses the captured native epoch throughout existing session-guarded activation.

A same-tool pending recovery record is self-healed only on a new explicit activation under the cross-process lock; incomplete file, credential or receipt cleanup remains non-ready with manual restore fallback.

Claude Desktop aliases are accepted only when derived from the current credential model set and resolve to exactly one real model, group and key before dispatch; Claude Code behavesAs never replaces the transmitted model ID.

processing.freshness: No retained cache or invented TTL; show local observation time. Clear selection on refresh and origin changes and reject older completions.
processing.recovery: Retry explicitly; all sensitive actions remain disabled and no rollback is necessary.
processing.correlation: Only the newest requestId and selected line may populate the panel.

pages.purpose: Select a tool and line, optionally read the public service catalog, select a group and real model ID, and inspect an unverified access preview without a credential or configuration write.
permissions: pure local deterministic preview projection only
public-service-catalog@v1 anonymous fixed-origin GET query after explicit user action

packages.objective: Make actual Codex relay use explicit and repair GUI-launched Node-backed tool execution, including DSH web Open, without changing remote services or packaging.
deliverables: Codex identity-versus-route copy and exact local-bridge route receipt presentation
Wrapper-preserving CLI discovery and bounded child runtime PATH resolution
Working DSH web startup and browser Open from the signed app GUI environment
Generalized runtime inheritance for the supported CLI terminal and isolated verification paths
Native, renderer and cross-platform regression evidence without installers
nonGoals: No server, NewAPI, account, billing, model entitlement, DNS, proxy-origin or remote deployment change
No package, version bump, signing, notarization, upload, release, updater artifact or update manifest
No auth.json overwrite, literal third-party token in Codex config, official-login removal or vendor binary patch
No force termination, user-session kill, global PATH mutation, shell command supplied by the renderer or claim that an AI self-description proves the route
allowedPaths: outputs/野菜API-Codex路由与CLI运行时修复.md

migrationPolicy.dataBackfill: No database, credential or receipt migration. Existing Codex and DSH receipts remain readable; a fresh explicit activation or Open uses the repaired runtime path.
migrationPolicy.rollback: Revert only this package's allowed source paths. Existing per-tool Restore original settings remains the user-facing configuration rollback; no server or data rollback exists.

compatibilityPolicy.strategy: Retain desktop-tool-activation@v10 and desktop-open-connection@v2 wire schemas. Strengthen runtime execution and user-facing evidence without changing request fields, token ownership, model IDs or receipt storage.
compatibilityPolicy.supportedVersions: Current native-discovered Codex 0.153.4-compatible desktop configuration and DSH 0.1.2-rc.1, plus wrapper-based supported CLI installations on macOS and Windows. Synthetic compile evidence does not claim every future vendor release.
compatibilityPolicy.removalGate: Do not return to canonical-script-only launch targets, inherited GUI PATH, account-display route inference, literal Codex keys, unbounded DSH startup or paid setup probes without a superseding decision and evidence.

requiredAcceptanceScenarios.assertion: Native fixtures prove wrapper identity is retained, bounded symlink parents are added only to child PATH, restricted-GUI-PATH DSH starts and returns a validated loopback URL, helper reuse remains owned, and no paid model prompt runs.

Renderer tests distinguish Codex official login identity from actual relay traffic, treat no bridge observation as unverified, label a bridge completion as confirmed Yeschoy relay use and show the exact gpt-6-astra model ID even when Codex abbreviates its own status label.

Typecheck, production renderer build, strict native tests/lint, Apple-Silicon compilation and Windows x64 compilation pass without creating or modifying an installer, release, server or updater artifact.

stopConditions: Codex custom-provider routing cannot be proven with current official configuration or a local synthetic receipt.
CLI launch would require a global PATH change, arbitrary renderer command, unsafe shell parsing, credential exposure or vendor binary patch.
DSH cannot be started and opened from a restricted GUI environment without a paid request or an unbounded wait.
Implementation requires server, NewAPI, account, billing, package, release, updater or public-distribution mutation.
